gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you seen my reading glasses?' he asked. He asked ___ his reading glasses.
gaps.explanation: 'If/whether' reports a yes/no question; the tense backshifts to past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the wet paint,' the caretaker warned us. The caretaker warned us ___ the wet paint.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands become not to + infinitive after told/asked/warned.

gaps.sentence: 'The delay is your fault,' the manager said to her. The manager ___ her for the delay.
gaps.explanation: Blame takes the pattern blame somebody for something.

gaps.sentence: 'Please don't smoke in here,' the host said. The host asked me ___ in there.
gaps.explanation: Negative requests: asked me not to smoke; 'here' shifts to 'there'.

gaps.sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
gaps.explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave the building immediately!' the firefighter ordered. The firefighter ordered us ___ the building immediately.
gaps.explanation: Orders are reported with order + object + to-infinitive.
